concept.title: Regularity of Bessel Distributions for Generic Representations of GL(n) over p-adic Fields
concept.concept_description: For any p-adic field F and any irreducible smooth admissible generic representation π of GL(n, F), the Bessel distribution B_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂} associated to Whittaker functionals is regular: there exists a unique smooth function j defined on a dense open subset of GL(n, F), locally integrable on GL(n, F), such that B_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂}(f) = ∫_{GL(n,F)} j(g)f(g)dg for all Schwartz functions f. This follows from the paper's main result (regularity follows from nontrivial bounds on Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups) combined with the known Deligne-Weil bounds on Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups of GL(n), which are products of smaller GL(m)'s.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any p-adic field F and any irreducible smooth admissible generic representation π of GL(n, F), the Bessel distribution B_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂} associated to Whittaker functionals is regular: there exists a unique smooth function j defined on a dense open subset of GL(n, F), locally integrable on GL(n, F), such that B_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂}(f) = ∫_{GL(n,F)} j(g)f(g)dg for all Schwartz functions f. This follows from the paper's main result (regularity follows from nontrivial bounds on Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups) combined with the known Deligne-Weil bounds on Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups of GL(n), which are products of smaller GL(m)'s.
concept.lean_guess: Apply the paper's conditional regularity theorem (Bessel distributions are regular provided Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups have nontrivial bounds) to GL(n). Since every Levi subgroup of GL(n) is isomorphic to a product ∏ GL(mᵢ) with ∑ mᵢ = n, the corresponding Kloosterman sums admit nontrivial bounds by Deligne's estimates from the Riemann hypothesis for varieties over finite fields (Weil II), yielding unconditional regularity for GL(n). The key intermediate step is formalizing the germ expansion of Kloosterman integrals and verifying the nontrivial bound condition for all Levi subgroups.

concept.title: Convex Position Minimizes Plane Graphs
concept.concept_description: For any set P of n ≥ 3 points in general position (no three collinear) in ℝ², the number of labeled plane graphs on P is at least the number of labeled plane graphs on n points in convex position. This formalizes the conjecture that, among all n-point configurations in general position, convex position yields the fewest plane graphs. The paper proves that configurations with convex hull of size O(n/log n) have Ω(12.24^n) plane graphs, strictly more than the ~11.65^n achieved by convex position, providing strong evidence for this conjecture.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any set P of n ≥ 3 points in general position (no three collinear) in ℝ², the number of labeled plane graphs on P is at least the number of labeled plane graphs on n points in convex position. This formalizes the conjecture that, among all n-point configurations in general position, convex position yields the fewest plane graphs. The paper proves that configurations with convex hull of size O(n/log n) have Ω(12.24^n) plane graphs, strictly more than the ~11.65^n achieved by convex position, providing strong evidence for this conjecture.
concept.lean_guess: Use the vertex potential framework from the paper to show that interior points (not on the convex hull) strictly increase the number of plane graphs relative to convex position. The potential φ(v) = deg(v) + vis(v) captures the local combinatorial richness at each vertex. The strategy would be: (1) establish that the expected potential of an interior vertex in a random plane graph strictly exceeds that of a hull vertex, (2) show this potential gap translates to a multiplicative increase in the total count of plane graphs, and (3) induct on the number of interior points, reducing to the base case of convex position. A key lemma would be that moving a hull point to the interior (while maintaining general position) strictly increases the plane graph count.

concept.concept_description: The paper proves that for a multiset P of n real numbers summing to zero (not all zero) and 1 ≤ k < n, the Shannon entropy of X_P (the sum of k elements sampled uniformly without replacement from P) satisfies H(X_P) ≥ H(Ber(k/n)). This conjecture asserts that the same inequality holds for Rényi entropy of order 2 (collision entropy): H₂(X_P) ≥ H₂(Ber(k/n)), equivalently, the collision probability of X_P is at most (k/n)² + (1−k/n)². Equality is achieved when P consists of one large positive value and n−1 equal negative values (e.g., P = {(n−1), −1, …, −1}), since then X_P is a scaled Bernoulli variable. The conjecture fails for min-entropy (α → ∞), as demonstrated by P = {1,1,−1,−1} with k=2 where max probability = 2/3 > 1/2, so the threshold α ≤ 2 is natural.
